## Context

The compact ticket summary drops the resolved alias and echoes the caller-supplied identifier. In representative agent workflows, this makes four-character prefixes locally salient even though aliases are available elsewhere. The resolver correctly fails closed on ambiguous prefixes.

## Proven root cause

summary_compute resolves each ticket through show_state but omits state alias from its return payload. The summary schema, library/MCP docs, and compact report therefore institutionalize an alias-free shape. Agent guidance also lacks an adjacent affirmative selection rule: use aliases for tracker commands after discovery, while reserving canonical UUIDs for identity-sensitive artifacts.

A pinned behavioral evaluation discriminated the causes. Prefix-only local summaries produced 25/25 four-character commands. Adding aliases locally produced 25/25 alias commands. Adding the affirmative rule independently produced 25/25 aliases. Removing the quick-reference example or historical four-character references did not change identifier selection. The negative control produced 25/25 full UUID rebar-ticket trailers.

## Repair plan

- Add the exact resolved alias as an additive field on every resolvable summary result while preserving the current ticket_id echo contract and unknown/ambiguous fail-closed behavior.
- Update the summary JSON schema plus library, MCP, CLI, and reference documentation to expose the alias consistently.
- Add adjacent affirmative AGENTS guidance to use aliases in tracker commands after discovery and full canonical UUIDs in rebar-ticket trailers and other identity-sensitive artifacts.
- Add held-out regression coverage through the core/library, CLI JSON, and MCP/schema surfaces, including an ambiguous-prefix control.
- Re-run the pinned behavioral evaluation and its canonical-trailer negative control after the repair.

## Testing

- Run `pytest tests/unit/test_summary_alias_b68c.py tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_outputs.py` for the executable and schema contracts.
- Run `make lint` and `make typecheck` for repository gates.
- Run `python /tmp/rebar_alias_eval.py` with the pinned model/settings to measure the agent-selection and canonical-trailer controls.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Core and library summary results expose the exact resolved alias, checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_summary_alias_b68c.py`.
- [x] CLI JSON summary output exposes the exact resolved alias, checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_summary_alias_b68c.py`.
- [x] MCP summary output conforms to the alias-bearing schema, checked by `pytest tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_outputs.py`.
- [x] Existing ticket_id echo semantics remain compatible, checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_summary_alias_b68c.py`.
- [x] Ambiguous prefixes remain fail-closed, checked by `pytest tests/unit/test_summary_alias_b68c.py`.
- [x] Agent guidance affirmatively prefers aliases for tracker commands, inspected in AGENTS.md.
- [x] Agent guidance reserves canonical UUIDs for identity-sensitive artifacts, inspected in AGENTS.md.
- [x] The held-out executable oracle is observed RED before the fix, GREEN after the fix, and RED again under alias-omission mutation.
- [x] The pinned agent-selection evaluation produces at least 23/25 alias commands with zero four-character prefixes, checked by `python /tmp/rebar_alias_eval.py`.
- [x] The negative control produces at least 23/25 full canonical UUID rebar-ticket trailers, checked by `python /tmp/rebar_alias_eval.py`.
